input-types-quiz-email.title: Choose an email field
input-types-quiz-email.prompt: Which input type best matches a field that collects an email address?
input-types-quiz-email.hint: Choose the type that describes the expected value.

help.concept: Input types give the browser useful information about the value being collected.
help.hint_1: Text can collect many values, but a more specific type exists.
help.hint_2: Use the dedicated email type for an email address.

input-types-quiz-choices.title: Distinguish checkbox and radio behavior
input-types-quiz-choices.hint: Think about whether choices are independent or mutually exclusive.

help.concept: Checkboxes represent independent selections; radio buttons with one shared name represent one choice from a group.
help.hint_1: One correct answer is about checkboxes.
help.hint_2: The other is about radio buttons that share a name.

options.a: Use checkboxes when several independent options may all be selected.
options.b: Give radio buttons the same name when they represent one choice from a group.
options.c: Use a date input for an email address.
options.d: Give every radio button the same id.

input-types-quiz-radio-order.title: Arrange an accessible radio group
input-types-quiz-radio-order.prompt: Arrange the tokens into a radio group with a group label and one connected option.
input-types-quiz-radio-order.hint: The fieldset wraps the group and legend describes it.

help.concept: Fieldset and legend identify the radio group, while label for connects to the unique input id.
help.hint_2: The input and its label belong before the closing fieldset.

input-types-quiz-blank.title: Complete an independent preference
input-types-quiz-blank.prompt: Choose the control that should fill the blank for an optional newsletter preference.
input-types-quiz-blank.hint: The preference can be selected independently.

help.concept: Checkbox is appropriate for an independent on/off preference.
help.hint_1: The id should match the label's for value.
help.hint_2: Keep a useful name so the preference has a key.

typed-data-controls.title: Use text, email, number, and date for the value you expect
typed-data-controls.bodyMarkdown:
The `type` attribute tells the browser what kind of value a one-line input is meant to collect. Use `text` for ordinary short text, `email` for an email address, `number` for numeric input, and `date` for a calendar date.

```html
<label for="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" name="email" type="email">
<label for="guests">Guests</label>
<input id="guests" name="guests" type="number">
```

Read this example line by line: the first label/input pair collects an email address, and the second pair collects a numeric guest count. Choosing a meaningful type gives the browser more context about the expected value.

checkbox-controls.title: Use checkbox when an option can be turned on or off independently
checkbox-controls.bodyMarkdown:
A checkbox represents an independent yes/no or on/off choice. Each checkbox should have its own label, and multiple checkboxes may all be selected at the same time.

```html
<input id="newsletter" name="newsletter" type="checkbox">
<label for="newsletter">Send me the newsletter</label>
```

Read the example line by line: the checkbox creates the independent choice, its id is `newsletter`, and the matching label explains exactly what selecting it means.

radio-controls.title: Give related radio buttons one shared name and a group label
radio-controls.bodyMarkdown:
Radio buttons are useful when the learner should choose exactly one option from a group. Give every radio button in the group the same `name`, give each one a unique `id` and `value`, and use `fieldset` with `legend` to describe the group.

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Session</legend>
  <input id="morning" name="session" type="radio" value="morning">
  <label for="morning">Morning</label>
  <input id="evening" name="session" type="radio" value="evening">
  <label for="evening">Evening</label>
</fieldset>
```

Read this example line by line: fieldset groups the choices, legend names the group, both radio inputs share `name="session"`, and each input has its own label through a unique id.
